ideas.title: The glossary opens with a table one guard reads
ideas.reading: docs/product/glossary.md:3 claims authority over code, copy and data model, but scripts/check-glossary.mjs (78 lines) only catches a decapitated entry, and scripts/check-repo.mjs registers it as the one 'glossary' guard among 48. The vocabulary that is actually held is held by two one-off scripts: check-soft-delete.mjs (Archive/Deactivate refused in both locales, ADR 20260820-every-delete-is-soft) and check-shop-word.mjs (10 Spanish rules quoted from src/i18n/locales/es-ES/README.md, each with a scope and an innocent-reading exclusion). check-shop-word.mjs's header records that the README's binding decisions 'do not stop them' and came back within a fortnight; check-soft-delete.mjs's header records that copy 'drifts toward the code that' names the storage model. .claude/rules/i18n.md:47 lists 'Vocabulary the guards refuse' as prose, and docs/agents/domain.md:27 asks agents to 'Use the glossary's vocabulary' with nothing behind it. The es-ES README's 17 sections are, in effect, the vocabulary contract en-US does not have; ls src/i18n/locales/en-US/ shows diver.json and staff/, no README.
ideas.idea: The glossary opens with one machine-readable table — one row per concept: the concept, its en-US screen word, its es-ES screen word, its storage and identifier word, its route segment, and the synonyms refused — and one guard, scripts/check-vocabulary.mjs, reads that table and refuses a listed synonym in any bundle value or key, route segment, or exported identifier, per locale, ratcheted at zero the way check-domain-strings.mjs is. check-shop-word.mjs and check-soft-delete.mjs become rows (el centro, la salida, la exención, Delete, Blocked/Ready, plaza) and are deleted as scripts; the es-ES README keeps its register and reasoning and hands its terminology tables to the glossary's Spanish column. check-glossary.mjs keeps its decapitation check and gains one rule: every table row has a bold entry, and every bold entry that names a screen word is a row. The grammar afterwards: a concept has at most two names — the storage name and the screen name — and the row is where a reader learns both; a third name anywhere is a guard failure, not a translation the reader performs.
ideas.dissolves: check-shop-word.mjs and check-soft-delete.mjs as separate scripts, the i18n.md 'Vocabulary the guards refuse' prose list, and the es-ES README as a second vocabulary of record.
ideas.scope: docs/product/glossary.md (head table); scripts/check-vocabulary.mjs + .test.mjs; scripts/check-repo.mjs rows 58, 70, 71; scripts/check-shop-word.mjs and scripts/check-soft-delete.mjs (deleted with their tests); .claude/rules/i18n.md; src/i18n/locales/es-ES/README.md; docs/agents/repo-checks.md; docs/agents/domain.md; one ADR superseding the guard halves of 20260820-every-delete-is-soft's enforcement note.

ADR 20260901-diveday-reimagined:168-171 says 'the lens vocabulary stays a lens' — but its ground is shape (a set, not a tag; single-select; never a safety signal; #1395), and no sentence of it defends the word. The diver's bearer pages say the ADR's own names to the diver: 'Your shelf' and 'Open your thread' (diver.shelf.title, diver.shelf.nextOpen, diver.notifications.shelfLink.*, 73 and 19 key names), while ADR 20260820-one-page-after-booking already made 'your trip' the one link and neither word has a glossary entry. docs/design/principles.md:121-126 says 'Never surface the implementation' and names 'our own process artifacts' explicitly. 'Board' is the staff tab at /schedule/board whose detail views are /trips/[id] (staff-destinations.ts:248-255), the lobby /board/[token] fed by src/db/departures-board.ts, and the trip_stage value 'boarding'.
ideas.idea: The contract's rule for these rows is that an internal name may live in an ADR, a table and a module, but the screen word is the shop's or the diver's, and the namespace and route carry the screen word: lenses.json becomes kindsOfDay.json beside the route that already says kinds-of-day, and trip_lenses becomes trip_kinds_of_day (H-49 makes the table rename a migration and nothing else), so 'lens' survives only in the ADR that coined it.
